Psychological Review, 125(5), 617?655. https://doi.org/10.1037/rev0000115

concrete_topics.title: Does witnessing online discrimination lead to decreased wellbeing in bystanders?
concrete_topics.topic_description: One of the most harmful effects of the current online environment is that it provides space for divisive or hateful content, targeting groups and individuals based on their ethnicity, gender, sexual orientation, or political views. The effects of hate speech on its targets have been extensively studied; however, the effect on bystanders remains less understood (c.f., Soral et al., 2019). Evidence from offline context suggests that knowledge of others' ethnic harassment is linked to deleterious occupational, health-related, and psychological consequences beyond those accounted for by direct harassment and affective disposition (Low, K. D., 2007). The Bc thesis should review empirical evidence about the link between exposure to online discrimination and wellbeing in bystanders, that is, people who are not directly targeted by discrimination. Please read: Hurd, N. M., Trawalter, S., Jakubow, A., Johnson, H. E., & Billingsley, J. T. (2022). Online racial discrimination and the role of white bystanders. American Psychologist, 77(1), 39?55. https://doi.org/10.1037/amp0000603 References: Low, K. D., Radhakrishnan, P., Schneider, K. T., & Rounds, J. (2007). The experiences of bystanders of workplace ethnic harassment. Journal of Applied Social Psychology, 37(10), 2261-2297. Soral, W., Bilewicz, M., & Winiewski, M. (2018). Exposure to hate speech increases prejudice through desensitization. Aggressive behavior, 44(2), 136-146.

concrete_topics.title: Perceiving Social Change: How Views of the Past and Future Shape Collective Action
concrete_topics.topic_description: The thesis will focus on the question: How do people respond to perceived backlash against social minorities? The primary focus will be on understanding whether perceiving a decline in the social acceptance and rights of one's group increases or decreases engagement in collective action. The thesis will examine the role of temporal perceptions?how people view their group's past, present, and future situation?and the emotions associated with these perceptions (e.g., anger, fear, hope, and nostalgia). As part of this thesis, you will identify and review studies on collective action, social change, and temporal perceptions, and examine how emotional reactions to perceived social progress or decline can motivate collective engagement. Please read: Lizzio?Wilson, M., Wenzel, M., Thomas, E. F., Osborne, D., & Skitka, L. J. (2025). What is, what was and what could be: Simultaneously comparing how emotional reactions to the past, present and future predict collective action. European Journal of Social Psychology, 55(7), 1369-1396.

concrete_topics.title: Reactions to Backlash Against Social Minorities: Mental Health, Wellbeing, and Resilience
concrete_topics.topic_description: The thesis will focus on the question: How do people, particularly LGBTIQ+ people, react to backlash against social minorities in terms of mental health outcomes, coping mechanisms, and resilience? The primary focus involves examining how hostile political and social environments shape psychological responses and well-being. As part of this thesis, you will focus on psychological theories related to minority stress, social identity threat, coping and resilience, community connectedness, or collective action. The thesis will focus on the question: How do people react to backlash against social minorities in terms of mental health outcomes, coping mechanisms, and resilience? The primary focus involves examining how hostile political and social environments shape psychological responses and well-being. As part of this thesis, you will focus on psychological theories related to minority stress, social identity threat, coping and resilience, community connectedness, or collective action. Please read: Flores, A., Strode, D., & Haider Markel, D. P. (2025). Political psychology and the study of LGBTQI+ groups, politics, and policy: Existing research and future directions. Political Psychology, 46, 213-249.

concrete_topics.title: Predictors of attitudes toward inequality reductions
concrete_topics.topic_description: In this thesis, you will look at the factors that predict people's attitudes toward measures (e.g., policies) aimed at reducing social inequalities. More specifically, you will focus on economic inequalities (wealth and income). The goal is to provide an overview of these factors and derive a systematization, describe methodological limitations of current approaches to studying such questions, and outline gaps that future research could aim to fill.

concrete_topics.title: Functioning in Recurrent depression
concrete_topics.topic_description: Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) is a highly prevalent and recurrent condition, with recurrence rates often exceeding 70?80% after successive episodes (Beshai et al., 2011; Monroe & Harkness, 2011). MDD contributes substantially to the global burden of disease and frequently results in functional impairment that persists even after symptomatic remission (Hardeveld et al., 2010; Sonino & Fava, 2012). A central debate in longitudinal research concerns whether post-remission functional limitations represent a ?scar? left by the depressive episode or reflect a pre-existing vulnerability that predisposes individuals to recurrence (Lewinsohn et al., 1981; Wichers et al., 2010).This systematic review examines the relationship between functioning and recurrent depression, with the aim of identifying prognostic factors associated with relapse and recurrence, as well as evaluating the effectiveness of function-focused interventions. To achieve this, the review proposes to analyze post-remission functional impairment using the conceptual framework of the International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health (ICF), an internationally recognized biopsychosocial model for describing health and disability (World Health Organization, 2001)

concrete_topics.title: Therapeutic Alliance measured by observer scales - can we see bonding in the patient and therapist behaviours?
concrete_topics.topic_description: In psychotherapy research, various rating scales are used to systematically assess and evaluate therapy sessions. A main aim of these types of rating procedures is to make therapeutic processes (e.g., alliance, emotional focus, use of techniques) measurable. The therapeutic alliance, typically defined as the collaborative and affective bond between therapist and client, is considered one of the most robust predictors of psychotherapy outcome across treatment modalities. It encompasses agreement on therapy goals, consensus on tasks, and the quality of the relational bond. Observer rating scales have been employed and assessed in numerous psychotherapy studies to shed light directly on alliance as it develops in-session. In this context, independent raters evaluate the therapeutic relationship based on video or audio recordings of psychotherapy sessions. The aim of this literature review is to examine which components of alliance are captured by these video rating scales, what psychometric properties they demonstrate, which features they offer in terms of practical applicability, and whether the results of these alliance-ratings show associations with treatment outcomes. The thesis language will be English or German

concrete_topics.title: Nicht jede Therapie verläuft gleich: Veränderungsverläufe in der Depressionsbehandlung
concrete_topics.topic_description: Psychotherapeutische Veränderungen verlaufen selten linear. Während einige Patient*innen bereits zu Beginn einer Behandlung deutliche Symptomverbesserungen zeigen, verändern sich andere langsamer oder erleben zwischenzeitliche Rückschläge. Solche Veränderungsverläufe (Change Trajectories) liefern wichtige Hinweise darauf, wie psychotherapeutische Veränderungen entstehen und welche Faktoren mit einem erfolgreichen Therapieverlauf zusammenhängen. In der Psychotherapieforschung kommen unterschiedliche Methoden zum Einsatz, um Veränderungen über die Zeit zu erfassen und typische Muster des Therapieverlaufs zu beschreiben. Das Ziel dieser Arbeit ist es, durch ein narratives Review die Literatur zu Veränderungsverläufen in der Behandlung von Depression zusammenzufassen. Dabei soll insbesondere untersucht werden, wie Veränderungsverläufe konzeptualisiert und erfasst werden, welche typischen Veränderungsmuster beschrieben werden und welche Erkenntnisse sich daraus für das Verständnis psychotherapeutischer Veränderungsprozesse ableiten lassen. Mögliche Schwerpunkte wären: - Welche Outcome- und Prozessvariablen (z. B. depressive Symptomatik, Funktionsniveau, therapeutische Allianz oder Emotionsregulation) werden typischerweise verwendet, um Veränderungsverläufe in der Depressionsbehandlung zu erfassen? - Welche typischen Veränderungsverläufe (z. B. frühe Verbesserung, graduelle Verbesserung, verzögerte Verbesserung oder Rückfälle) werden in der Literatur beschrieben? - Welche Prädiktoren unterschiedlicher Veränderungsverläufe wurden in der Literatur identifiziert? - Welche methodischen Ansätze werden verwendet, um Veränderungsverläufe während einer Depressionsbehandlung zu untersuchen (z. B. Growth-Curve-Modelle, Growth Mixture Models oder Latent Class Growth Analysis)? Die Arbeit kann sowohl auf Deutsch als auch auf Englisch verfasst werden.

concrete_topics.title: Einstellungen in der Allgemeinbevölkerung gegenüber digitalen Gesundheitsanwendungen (DiGa) zur Behandlung psychischer Symptome oder Störungen
concrete_topics.topic_description: Digitalen Gesundheitsanwendungen (DGa) und Selbsthilfe-Apps wird ein grosses Potenzial für eine bessere Versorgung von Menschen mit psychischen Problemen oder Störungen attestiert. In einigen Ländern, wie bspw. Deutschland, können DGa mittlerweile auf Rezept verschrieben werden. Um in der Gesundheitsversorgung eine nachhaltige Wirkung zu erzielen, müssen innovative Angebote wie DGa sorgfältig in das Gesundheitssystem integriert werden und sollten auf eine hohe Akzeptanz bei den betroffenen Personenkreisen stossen. Im Rahmen einer systematischen Übersichtsarbeit soll in der vorliegenden Bachelorarbeit der Stand aktueller ? möglichst bevölkerungsrepräsentativer ? Umfragen zur Akzeptanz und den Einstellungen in der Allgemeinbevölkerung gegenüber DGa zusammengefasst und methoden-kritisch aufgearbeitet werden. Dabei sollen mögliche Einflussgrössen herausgearbeitet werden, wie bspw. Alter, Geschlecht und sozioökonomische Unterschiede. Die Arbeit soll in deutscher oder englischer Sprache und nach gängigen Standards zur Erstellung von systematic reviews verfasst werden.

concrete_topics.title: Stressreaktivität und Depression
concrete_topics.topic_description: Depressive Störungen sind durch eine hohe Rückfall- und Rezidivneigung gekennzeichnet. Das Verständnis der zugrunde liegenden psychologischen und biologischen Vulnerabilitätsmechanismen ist zentral, um Risikoprozesse besser zu verstehen. Ein Mechanismus der in diesem Zusammenhang untersucht wurde, ist die Stressreaktivität. Diese beschreibt, wie stark und in welcher Form Individuen auf belastende Ereignisse reagieren (biologisch, psychologische). Erhöhte Stressreaktivität nicht nur mit dem Auftreten depressiver Episoden assoziiert ist, sondern auch als Vulnerabilitätsmechanismus für Rückfälle und Rezidive. Ziel dieser Bachelorarbeit ist es, den aktuellen Forschungsstand zur Rolle von Stressreaktivität im Kontext depressiver Störungen systematisch zu erfassen und einzuordnen. Dabei soll untersucht werden, wie Stressreaktivität in der Literatur gemessen und berücksichtigt wurde und in welchem Zusammenhang sie mit dem Verlauf der Depression stehen. Die konkrete Fokussierung und Ausarbeitung der Forschungsfrage erfolgt im Verlauf der Arbeit auf Basis der identifizierten Studienlage. Die Arbeit kann auf Englisch oder Deutsch verfasst werden.

concrete_topics.title: Vocational training programs that incorporate psychosocial interventions in both low-income and high-income settings
concrete_topics.topic_description: Youth is a critical developmental period associated with increased risk for the onset of mental health conditions. With youth unemployment at historically high levels, particularly in regions such as Sub-Saharan Africa, vocational training programs provide practical pathways to employment while also offering an opportunity to support young peoples mental health and psychosocial well-being. What psychosocial interventions have been implemented in vocational training programs globally, and what potential do they show? language: english

concrete_topics.title: Cross-cultural measures and theories well-being
concrete_topics.topic_description: Much of the existing research on well-being has been developed in the Global North and is grounded in Western frameworks of what it means to live well and thrive. What culturally grounded frameworks, theories, and measures of well-being exist across diverse contexts, and where are the major gaps in current research? language: english

concrete_topics.title: Household-level interventions for mental health care in low-middle income countries - delivery models, effectiveness, and research gaps
concrete_topics.topic_description: In many contexts, the family is the primary unit through which health is understood, managed, and supported. Understanding mental health burden at the household level may help to explain the clustering of risk and the unmet need within families, ultimately helping to identify novel avenues for intervention. What house-hold level interventions for mental health exist in low-middle income countries, and how effective are they? language: english

concrete_topics.title: Dynamic Systems Theories
concrete_topics.topic_description: Dynamic systems theories (DST) offer a powerful framework for understanding psychological processes, emphasizing the complexity and adaptability of human behavior. These theories are particularly relevant for exploring developmental processes, social interactions, and personality dynamics, providing insights into how patterns emerge and evolve over time. This bachelor thesis will focus on dynamic systems theories in psychology, allowing students to explore a specific area of interest. Potential focus areas include developmental psychology, social psychology, or personality research, among others. The task involves a thorough literature review, with an emphasis on theoretical frameworks, methodological innovations, and practical applications of DST. Students are encouraged to critically evaluate how DST contributes to understanding dynamic processes in their chosen domain and discuss its implications for future research. The thesis can be written in English or German.

concrete_topics.title: Regularized Estimation In Psychology
concrete_topics.topic_description: Regularization methods have gained prominence in psychological research as tools to address challenges such as high-dimensional data, multicollinearity, and overfitting. These techniques, which originated in fields like machine learning and biostatistics, are now being adapted to improve predictive accuracy and enhance model interpretability in psychological studies. Applications range from feature selection in large-scale datasets to stabilizing estimates in complex models. This bachelor thesis will focus on the use of regularization methods in psychology, offering a literature review of current approaches and their potential to address unique challenges in the field. The review may include applications in subfields like decision science, clinical psychology, or personality assessment, as well as discussions on general trends and usage patterns. The aim is to critically review how regularization is used and can enhance or hinder psychological research methodologies, potentially considering insights from related disciplines such as biostatistics. The thesis can be written in English or German.

concrete_topics.title: Deep Learning In Psychology
concrete_topics.topic_description: Deep learning has emerged as a powerful tool for predictive modeling in fields such as computer vision and natural language processing. While its applications in psychology remain limited, its potential for advancing psychological research is considerable. Deep learning techniques, including feedforward neural networks (FNNs), recurrent neural networks (RNNs), and convolutional neural networks (CNNs), offer innovative approaches to analyzing complex psychological data. These methods allow for capturing patterns and relationships that traditional statistical models may overlook. This bachelor thesis will explore the application of deep learning in psychological research. The focus may be on specific application areas, such as personality psychology, cognitive modeling, or mental health diagnostics, or on general trends and usage patterns of deep learning across the discipline. The aim is to provide a comprehensive literature review, considering the benefits, limitations, and challenges of integrating deep learning techniques into psychological research. Practical examples and discussions from existing literature will serve as a foundation for understanding how these methods can address prediction-focused research questions in psychology. The thesis can be written in English or German.

concrete_topics.title: Controveries In Cross-Lagged Panel Modelling
concrete_topics.topic_description: Cross-lagged panel modeling (CLPM) is a statistical technique widely used in psychology to investigate reciprocal causal relationships in longitudinal data. Historically favored for its simplicity, the CLPM has faced criticism for its inability to distinguish within-person dynamics from stable between-person differences. This has led to the development of alternative approaches, such as the random-intercept CLPM, which aim to address these limitations by incorporating stable-trait components. The controversy surrounding CLPM centers on its relevance and appropriateness for answering various psychological research questions. Advocates of the CLPM argue it is well-suited for studying stable, individual-level processes, while critics highlight its susceptibility to biased or spurious causal effect estimates. This bachelor thesis will explore the ongoing debate about the CLPM and its alternatives, critically examining the theoretical and methodological implications of these approaches. The focus will include understanding the conditions under which different models perform best, the impact of research design choices, and the role of timescale in studying psychological processes. The thesis aims to provide a comprehensive literature review on the topic, offering insights into how these methodological controversies influence the interpretation of longitudinal psychological data. The thesis can be written in English or German.

concrete_topics.title: Flexible measures in decision-making under risk and uncertainty
concrete_topics.topic_description: Recent analyses suggested a "proliferation of measures" in psychological research. Alike, in research on risk taking many different tasks are used to measure decision making under risk and uncertainty. But how consistently or flexibility are these tasks implemented? And how do potential differences in task implementation impact research findings?

concrete_topics.title: Psychological processes involved in behavioral tasks of risk taking
concrete_topics.topic_description: Diverse tasks have been developed to test people's willingness to take risks. But do they all tap the same psychological processes? Or do they tap into different processes that reflect different aspects of risk-taking behavior?

concrete_topics.title: The use of LLMs in psychological research
concrete_topics.topic_description: Large Langugage Models (LLM) are powerful tools for discovering patterns in written text and speech. How are they applied in psychology, and what techniques are available for psychological research? The goal of this project is to review and identify the various LLM methods used in psychological research, and to provide insight into the potential applications for the study of complex processes in psychology.

concrete_topics.title: Time frame of risky choices
concrete_topics.topic_description: People make countless choices every day. Some of these choices are made in a matter of seconds, others need consideration lasting for hours, sometimes days. One factor determining the duration of a choice might be the psychological mechanisms that are at play. The goal of this project is to review how long different (classes of) psychological processes take to unfold and for how long they may exert an influence on a person's choices.

concrete_topics.title: Mortality and morbidity after loss: review of the literature
concrete_topics.topic_description: A literature review of health outcomes and death rates after bereavement

concrete_topics.title: Motivation, learning and grief
concrete_topics.topic_description: Review of the literature

concrete_topics.title: Developing Social Brains
concrete_topics.topic_description: How do social brains develop and how do social relations shape our brains? In this thesis, the fundamental processes of human brain development are discussed in relation to human relationships (parents, siblings, peers, etc.) in order to review current knowledge about how our cognition or affect develops in relation to the social experiences we make. Literature: Falk, E. B., & Bassett, D. S. (2017). Brain and social networks: fundamental building blocks of human experience. Trends in cognitive sciences, 21(9), 674-690.

concrete_topics.title: The development of the neural correlates of mentalizing in children
concrete_topics.topic_description: Theory of Mind (ToM) or mentalizing is a basic social skill which is characterized by our ability of perspective-taking and the understanding of cognitive and emotional states of others. ToM development is essential to successfully navigate in various social contexts. The neural basis of mentalizing is well-studied in adults, however, less evidence exists in children. This bachelor thesis will summarize the existing evidence on fMRI studies investigating mentalizing or Theory of Mind in childhood and adolescence. Investigations will further target both healthy development and the neural correlates of mentalizing in children and adolescence with neuropsychiatric diagnosis.

concrete_topics.title: Intergenerational transfer effects on emotion processing and regulation in parents and their children
concrete_topics.topic_description: Socioemotional abilities represent different skill sets of social and emotional functioning. These skills are fundamental to our every day life and associated with our physical and psychological well-being. Socioemotional skill acquisition starts early in life and strongly rely on early social experiences such as caregiver-child relationships or dyadic learning. What are the intergenerational transfer effects on emotion processing and emotion regulation? What are the intergenerational transfer effects on emotion processing and regulation as observed in a child's behavior? What are the intergenerational transfer effects on emotion processing and regulation as observed in a child's biology? What are the function of intergenerational transfer effects and how are these connected to adaptive and maladaptive functioning, particularly during stressful life events? What are the intergenerational transfer effects on socioemotional functioning in children when their parents have to deal with challenging life circumstances? These are just some of the questions that could be chosen to being elaborated more on in a bachelor thesis.

concrete_topics.title: Human-AI Teaming: Was macht Teams mit einer künstlichen Intelligenz als Teammitglied effektiv?
concrete_topics.topic_description: Künstliche Intelligenz (KI) erobert mit zunehmender Geschwindigkeit neue Einsatzgebiete. Berichte über die Entdeckung neuer Zusammenhänge, die KI beispielsweise anhand von selbsterlernten Regeln aus riesigen Datenmengen hervorbringt, sind inzwischen annähernd alltäglich. Angesichts dieser Entwicklung wird KI nicht mehr nur als Werkzeug, das von Menschen bei ihrer Arbeit beispielsweise in der Medizin, dem Personalwesen oder der Finanzbranche genutzt werden kann, deklariert, sondern erhält immer häufiger die Zuschreibung der Rolle eines Teammitglieds. In dieser Funktion kann KI als eine zum autonomen Handeln befähigte Entität proaktiv zu Teamprozessen beitragen und so Arbeitsergebnisse beeinflussen. Ein Beispiel für diese Entwicklung in der Praxis ist die Kollaborationsplattform Microsoft Teams. Dort ist in Teamkanälen inzwischen der Einsatz von KI-basierten Chatrobotern gängig, die in ihrer einfachsten Form Termine für Teammeetings einstellen oder Arbeitsschritte zusammenfassen. Sogenanntes "AI-Teaming" (Teamarbeit mit einer künstlichen Intelligenz als Teammitglied) bringt aber auch neue Herausforderungen. Natürlich können KI-Teammitglieder (noch) nicht dieselben Verhaltensweisen zeigen wie ein menschliches Teammitglied. In dieser Bachelorarbeit soll erarbeitet werden, was ein Mensch-KI Team effektiv macht. Dazu sollen aktuelle Modelle zu Human-AI Teaming zusammengefasst werden und mit aktuellen empirischen Studien ergänzt werden. Es werden verschiedene Arbeiten in diesem Themenbereich angeboten. Der Fokus der Arbeit kann eingegrenzt werden (Z. B. Fokus auf Vertrauen in KI, Koordination, Kommunikation mit KI etc.).

concrete_topics.title: Verspieltheit und Humor am Arbeitsplatz
concrete_topics.topic_description: Basierend auf dem Spiel beschreibt Verspieltheit (engl. Playfulness) eine intrinsische Motivation des Spielens. Verspieltheit ist eine Art humorvolles Klima einer entspannten Arbeitsplatzatmosphäre des Vergnügens, Lachens und Humors. Verspieltheit umfasst fünf Dimensionen: physische Spontanität, soziale Spontanität, kognitive Spontanität, manifeste Freude und Sinn für Humor. Studien haben gezeigt, dass Verspieltheit positive Effekte für Individuen und Teams am Arbeitsplatz haben kann. Diese Bachelorarbeit betrachtet Verspieltheit im Arbeitskontext und identifiziert die Auswirkungen von Verspieltheit auf individuelle und Teamergebnisse. Die Arbeit fokussiert sich auf Verspieltheit bei Erwachsenen im Arbeitskontext und soll von Verspieltheit im Kindesalter abgegrenzt werden. Es werden verschiedene Arbeiten in diesem Bereich angeboten. Je nach Interesse kann der Fokus auf individuelle Outcomes (Arbeitszufriedenheit, Produktivität etc.) oder Teamoutcomes untersucht werden. Zudem kann Playfulness als grösseres Konzept oder Humor an sich gewählt werden.

concrete_topics.title: (Relational) Savoring in Daily Life
concrete_topics.topic_description: Savoring beschreibt das bewusste in Erinnerung rufen und auskosten vergangener positiver Momente. Relational savoring ist eine beziehungsorientierte Form davon, welche sich auf positive Momente mit nahen Beziehungspersonen fokussiert. Durch (relational) savoring werden positive Erinnerungen reflektiert und die Momente erneut durchlebt, wodurch die damit verbundenen positiven Emotionen verstärkt und das Wohlbefinden gefördert werden soll. In intensiven Längsschnittstudien, sogenannten ecological momentary assessments (EMA) oder auch Tagebuchstudien, werden Studienteilnehmende über einen gewissen Zeitraum täglich oder mehrmals am Tag befragt. In dieser Bachelorarbeit soll die bestehende Literatur zu (relational) savoring in EMA-Studien systematisch zusammengetragen werden. Dabei soll eine Übersicht über die verwendeten Designs (bspw. daily diary, weekly diary) sowie die untersuchten Zusammenhänge mit Variablen wie Gesundheit und Wohlbefinden herausgearbeitet werden. Die Bachelorarbeit kann auf Deutsch oder Englisch verfasst werden.

concrete_topics.title: (Relational) Savoring in Interventionsstudien
concrete_topics.topic_description: Savoring beschreibt das bewusste in Erinnerung rufen und auskosten vergangener positiver Momente. Relational savoring ist eine beziehungsorientierte Form davon, welche sich auf positive Momente mit nahen Beziehungspersonen fokussiert. Savoring-Interventionen zielen darauf ab, solche positiven Erinnerungen zu reflektieren und die Momente erneut zu durchleben, wodurch die damit verbundenen positiven Emotionen verstärkt und das Wohlbefinden gefördert werden soll. Savoring Interventionen wurden in bisherigen Studien mit unterschiedlichen Methoden (z. B. schriftliche Erinnerungsaufgabe vs. mündliche Erzählung), Formaten (z.B. Onlineintervention vs. in-person) und Intensitäten (einmalige vs. mehrmalige Induktion) umgesetzt. In dieser Bachelorarbeit soll systematisch zusammengetragen werden, wie (relational) savoring in bisheriger Forschung in Interventionsstudien umgesetzt wurde. Dabei sollen die Effekte auf verschiedene Outcomes sowie Faktoren, die für die Effektivität von (relational) savoring Interventionen relevant sind, herausgearbeitet werden. Die Bachelorarbeit kann auf Deutsch oder Englisch verfasst werden.

concrete_topics.title: The third man factor across the globe: How do non-ordinary experiences get expressed through cultural scripts.
concrete_topics.topic_description: Non-ordinary experiences, including the "third man factor" (sensing an unseen presence during extreme situations), mystical experiences, and altered states of consciousness, appear across all cultures but are interpreted and expressed through different cultural lenses. This literature review will examine how cultural scripts, religious frameworks, and local meaning systems shape the reporting, interpretation, and integration of non-ordinary experiences. The thesis should explore cross-cultural variations in how these experiences are conceptualized, valued, and incorporated into personal and collective narratives. This work should be written in English. Relevant Literature: Maraldi, E.O., Taves, A., Moll, J. et al. Nonordinary Experiences, Well-being and Mental Health: A Systematic Review of the Evidence and Recommendations for Future Research. J Relig Health 63, 410?444 (2024). https://doi.org/10.1007/s10943-023-01875-8 Taves, A., & Barlev, M. (2023). A feature-based approach to the comparative study of ?nonordinary? experiences. American Psychologist, 78(1), 50?61. https://doi.org/10.1037/amp0000990

concrete_topics.title: The historical psychology of emotion language
concrete_topics.topic_description: The language we use to name and describe emotions is not fixed: emotion concepts, and the words that carry them, shift across historical time, and a term that seems stable can change in meaning, salience, and value from one era to the next. Drawing on the emerging field of historical psychology, this review will in a structured fashion examine how the language of emotion has changed over historical time and what this reveals about emotional life, focusing on: (1) the theoretical and methodological foundations of historical psychology, including the use of large historical text corpora to reconstruct past mental life, along with the assumptions and limitations of this approach; (2) documented historical shifts in emotion vocabularies and in the frequency, valence, and expression of emotion words across centuries; (3) what such changes imply for debates about the universality versus the historical and cultural construction of emotion, and for how words of similar meaning come to be valued differently across periods and contexts. This work should be written in English. Relevant Literature: Atari, M., & Henrich, J. (2023). Historical psychology. Current Directions in Psychological Science, 32(2), 176?183. https://doi.org/10.1177/09637214221149737 Morin, O., & Acerbi, A. (2017). Birth of the cool: A two-centuries decline in emotional expression in Anglophone fiction. Cognition and Emotion, 31(8), 1663?1675. https://doi.org/10.1080/02699931.2016.1260528

concrete_topics.title: Convergent or Conflicting? Comparing the Major Axes of Cross-Cultural Variation and Their Antecedents
concrete_topics.topic_description: Cross-cultural psychology has produced a proliferation of dimensions intended to capture systematic variation between societies, including individualism?collectivism, tightness?looseness, power distance, and relational mobility, among others. While each axis was developed to explain distinct patterns of behavior, cognition, and social organization, they frequently draw on overlapping theoretical foundations and, in some cases, generate competing or contradictory predictions for the same outcomes. This literature review will synthesize the major cultural axes by examining their theoretical origins, the empirical predictors and antecedents proposed for each (such as ecological, historical, economic, and pathogen-related factors), and the degree to which these constructs converge or diverge. The thesis should critically compare where the axes make redundant, complementary, or conflicting predictions, clarify the conceptual boundaries between them, and assess whether they are best understood as distinct dimensions or as partial reflections of a smaller set of underlying factors. The review should give particular attention to cases in which two or more axes predict opposing effects, and to how the field has attempted to adjudicate such tensions empirically. This work should be written in English. Minkov, M., & Kaasa, A. (2022). Do dimensions of culture exist objectively? A validation of the revised Minkov-Hofstede model of culture with World Values Survey items and scores for 102 countries. Journal of International Management, 28(4), Article 100971. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.intman.2022.100971 Kaasa, A., & Minkov, M. (2022). Are different two-dimensional models of culture just a matter of different rotations? Evidence from the analysis based on the WVS/EVS. Journal of Cross-Cultural Psychology, 53(2), 127?156. https://doi.org/10.1177/00220221211072790

concrete_topics.title: Measuring Equanimity: Conceptualization, Operationalization, and Predictors in Psychological Research
concrete_topics.topic_description: Equanimity, broadly conceived as an even-minded, non-reactive stance toward experience that remains stable across pleasant, unpleasant, and neutral states, has gained increasing attention in psychological research, particularly within the study of contemplative practice and well-being. Despite this growing interest, the construct is operationalized inconsistently, is often conflated with related notions such as mindfulness, acceptance, emotion regulation, and affective flattening, and is assessed through a heterogeneous set of self-report instruments with varying conceptual assumptions. This literature review will examine how equanimity has been defined and measured in psychological research, comparing existing scales and methodologies with respect to their underlying conceptualizations, psychometric properties, and discriminant validity relative to neighboring constructs. The thesis should additionally survey the proposed predictors and correlates of equanimity, including contemplative training, dispositional traits, and emotion-regulatory processes, and evaluate the extent to which measurement choices shape the conclusions drawn about its antecedents. The review should highlight points of conceptual disagreement and consider what an adequate operationalization of equanimity would require. This work should be written in English. Desbordes G, Gard T, Hoge EA, Hölzel BK, Kerr C, Lazar SW, Olendzki A, Vago DR. Moving beyond Mindfulness: Defining Equanimity as an Outcome Measure in Meditation and Contemplative Research. Mindfulness (N Y). 2014 Jan 21;2014(January):356?72. doi: 10.1007/s12671-013-0269-8. PMID: 25750687; PMCID: PMC4350240. An?layo, B. Relating Equanimity to Mindfulness. Mindfulness 12, 2635?2644 (2021). https://doi.org/10.1007/s12671-021-01671-z

concrete_topics.title: Stoicism or stoicism: How psychologists construct and measure philosophical beliefs
concrete_topics.topic_description: Right now, Stoicism is experiencing a revival, both in popular understandings and in psychological research. Nevertheless, psychologist and philosophers have a difficult time agreeing on what is being talked about under the label of Stoicism. This thesis aims to track the conceptual evolution and measurement of Stoicism in psychology through a literature review to understand how psychologists use lay understandings and existing labels to derive new constructs. This work should be written in English. Relevant literature: LeBon, T., Brown, G., DiGiuseppe, R. et al. The Development and Validation of the Stoic Attitudes and Behaviours Scale. Cogn Ther Res (2025). https://doi.org/10.1007/s10608-025-10635-9 Karl, J. A., Verhaeghen, P., Aikman, S. N., Solem, S., Lassen, E. R., & Fischer, R. (2022). Misunderstood stoicism: The negative association between stoic ideology and well-being. Journal of Happiness Studies: An Interdisciplinary Forum on Subjective Well-Being, 23(7), 3531?3547. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10902-022-00563-w

concrete_topics.title: The state of historical psychology: What empirical tools are being used to understand historical texts in psychology.
concrete_topics.topic_description: Psychology is increasingly recognizing the value of historical texts as data source to understand past societies and gain a long-term understanding of psychological dynamics. The aim of this thesis is to write a systematic literature review which summarizes the state of the art how psychologists have gone and are going about extracting psychological information from text. This work has to be written in English. Relevant Literature Atari, M., & Henrich, J. (2023). Historical Psychology. Current Directions in Psychological Science, 32(2), 176-183. https://doi.org/10.1177/09637214221149737 (Original work published 2023) Du, A. H., Karl, J. A., Fetvadjiev, V., Luczak-Roesch, M., Pirngruber, R., & Fischer, R. (2023). Tracing the evolution of personality cognition in early human civilisations: A computational analysis of the Gilgamesh epic. European Journal of Personality, 38(2), 274-290. https://doi.org/10.1177/08902070231161869 (Original work published 2024)

process.process_description: Wer eine Bachelorarbeit buchen will, muss vor der Buchung die Zusage der gewünschten Betreuungsperson einholen (vgl. §26 der Studienordnung, allg. Teil) — indem Sie die Betreuungsperson oder den Studienprogrammdirektor (Rico Valär) kontaktieren. Nach Zusage buchen Sie das 15‑ECTS‑Modul über das Studierendenportal. Nach Ende der Buchungsfrist erhalten Sie vom Dekanat einen Link zu einer Website, auf der sofort Betreuungsperson und provisorischer Titel zu registrieren sind. Das Modul dauert ein Semester; Mindestlänge: 65’000 Zeichen inkl. Leerschläge. Als Betreuerinnen/Betreuer kommen ordentliche/ausserordentliche Professor*innen, Assistenzprofessor*innen, Titularprofessor*innen und Privatdozierende in Frage. Andere Mitarbeitende mit Doktorat benötigen Vorgesetzten‑Zustimmung und einen Antrag an die Studienprogrammdirektorin/den Studienprogrammdirektor. Abgabefristen: für HS-Bewertung bis 1. Dezember, für FS-Bewertung bis 1. Juni; Verlängerungsgesuche an Betreuungsperson und Sven Bachmann.

Any student who wants to book a Masterarbeit must first obtain the supervisor’s written consent (gem. §31 Studienordnung, allg. Teil) — contact the desired supervisor or the study program director Rico Valär. After consent, book the thesis like any module during normal booking periods in the Studierendenportal. After the booking deadline the Philosophical Faculty will send a link to a special website where you must immediately register the supervisor and a provisional title. The Master thesis is a two‑semester module (can be assessed after one semester by agreement). Minimum length: 120,000 characters including spaces. Eligible supervisors: full and associate professors, assistant professors, titular professors and Privatdozierende; other staff with a PhD may supervise after superior’s approval and an application to the program director. Deadlines: submit to supervisor by 1 Dec for HS grading, 1 June for FS grading; extension requests go to the supervisor and Sven Bachmann. Official rule reference: §31 of the Studienordnung (general part).

Studierende im Major-Studienprogramm schließen das Bachelorstudium mit einer Bachelorarbeit zu einem selbstgewählten Thema ab. Die Arbeit ist auf ein Semester begrenzt (Modul „Bachelorarbeit“); frühzeitiger Kontakt zur gewünschten Betreuungsperson ist Pflicht — dieser Kontakt muss vor der Buchung erfolgen. Formale Vorgaben: Sprache Deutsch (Ausnahmen: Französisch, Englisch, Italienisch), Umfang 35–40 Seiten (detaillierte Vorgaben in den Merkblättern/Leitfäden). Den Abschluss müssen Studierende termingerecht bei der Philosophischen Fakultät beantragen; nähere Angaben dazu finden sich auf der Homepage des Studiendekanats. Offizielle Hinweise und Vorlagen sind als Downloads verfügbar (Titelblatt, Anleitung der Philosophischen Fakultät, Merkblätter/Leitfäden).

This unit supervises Bachelor theses for students in the Filmwissenschaft Major (120 ECTS). Choose a realistic film‑scholarship topic early, contact a prüfungsberechtigte Betreuungsperson (professors, postdocs, Oberassistierende or Privatdozierende listed on the FIWI team page), send an idea sketch and arrange a meeting before booking the “Bachelorarbeit” module; timing of the booking is agreed with the supervisor. Work proceeds via a concept phase (short concept, max ~5 pages with summary, question, theory, thesis, method, provisional structure, bibliography/filmography), a writing phase (allow ≥1 month for first draft and ≥2 weeks for revision) and final submission to the supervisor within the deadline. Formals: 35–40 pages (70’000–80’000 characters), normally in German (English/French by agreement). Official guidelines and templates: FIWI Download/Bildung (Studium) and the Faculty module page (https://www.phil.uzh.ch/de/studium/rundumsstudium/module.html).

Students enrolled in the MA Major 90 or Mono 120 (Network Cinema CH) complete the Master by booking two modules independently: a one‑semester Fachüberblick (60‑min oral exam, typically CW 18–19 in FS or 48–49 in HS) and a two‑semester Masterarbeit. Choose and define your topic early, contact a prüfungsberechtigte Betreuungsperson (professors, postdocs, Oberassistierende or Privatdozierende listed on the FIWI team page) before booking, send an idea sketch and arrange a meeting; after acceptance agree on timeline and the timing of the module booking. Prepare a concept paper (ideally ≤8 pages excluding provisional outline, bibliography, filmography) with summary, question, theory, thesis, method and corpus. Regular attendance of the Master‑Kolloquium over two semesters (≈3–4 sessions/semester) is required. Binding rules and deadlines are on the Philosophical Faculty site (password‑protected masterarbeit area): https://www.phil.uzh.ch/de/studium/rundumsstudium/module.html.

Masterstudierende der MA‑Studienrichtung schreiben eine Masterarbeit (30 ETCS Credits). Vor der formellen Buchung des Moduls muss frühzeitig Kontakt mit der gewünschten Betreuungsperson aufgenommen werden; nach der Buchung stehen zwei Semester für die Arbeit zur Verfügung. Der Besuch des begleitenden Kolloquiums für Masterarbeiten ist während beider Semester obligatorisch und bereitet auf Präsentation und Verteidigung vor. Formale Vorgaben: Sprache Deutsch (in Ausnahmefällen Französisch, Englisch oder Italienisch), Umfang 60–80 Seiten, zeitliche Limitierung zwei Semester. Für die Anmeldung zum Abschluss, detaillierte Merkblätter und Leitfäden sowie alle relevanten Informationen ist die Homepage des Studiendekanats bzw. die Seite «Anmeldung zum Abschluss» zuständig.

Masterstudierende buchen das zweisemestrige Modul «Masterarbeit (06SM240-MA)» selbst während der Modulbuchungszeit; das Modul ist nicht mit einer Lehrveranstaltung verbunden. Umfang und Thema sind vorgängig mit einer Betreuungsperson zu klären; die formalen und inhaltlichen Anforderungen werden dort festgelegt. Nach Ablauf der Buchungsfrist fordert das Studiendekanat die Studierenden auf, zunächst einen provisorischen und später den endgültigen Titel sowie die Betreuungsperson einzutragen. Die Masterarbeit muss spätestens im auf das Buchungssemester folgenden Semester abgegeben werden (Laufzeit 2 Semester); frühere Abgabe nach einem Semester ist möglich. Abgabe elektronisch an die Betreuungsperson (optional zusätzlich in Papier). Abgabefristen: 01. Dezember (Herbstsemester) und 01. Juni (Frühjahrssemester). Zur Betreuung berechtigt sind die aufgelisteten Institutspersonen; auch Mitarbeitende mit Doktorgrad können angefragt werden. Offizielle Hinweise und Termine: phil.uzh.ch/Abschluss. Fragen an programmkoordination@soziologie.uzh.ch oder abschluss@phil.uzh.ch.

Bachelor students complete a 15‑ECTS empirical Bachelorarbeit based on a quantitative data analysis. The Bachelorarbeitsmodul bildet den Betreuungsrahmen; die Arbeit wird angeleitet und moderiert durch die Dozierenden des Instituts (i.e., supervision is provided by institute lecturers). Registration, booking, submission and deadlines are not given on this page — you must follow the Philosophische Fakultät – Abschluss webpage for the formal Anmeldung, Fristen and submission procedures. Formal requirements noted here: independent empirical work with quantitative analysis; see the Merkblatt Bachelor‑Arbeit (PDF, Stand 09.01.2026). Official guidelines include the faculty Abschluss page and the Bachelor Studienordnung. Questions: programmkoordination@soziologie.uzh.ch or abschluss@phil.uzh.ch.

Eligible students are those in the Major Soziologie who have completed the statistical-method training (Statistics 1 and especially Statistics 2; Statistics 3 recommended). To register, book the module "Bachelorarbeit" (240-BAa, 15 ECTS) and attend the accompanying weekly four‑hour seminar; only book after passing the required statistics modules. Your thesis must be an independent empirical paper based on quantitative analysis (≈450 working hours for 15 ECTS); R and Stata are supported; common datasets are SHP or ESS (self‑collected data possible with a short exposé). Supervision is provided by the course instructors—contact them in advance to discuss topics and data and nominate one as supervisor to the Studiendekanat when requested (usually after course start). Exact deadlines, session details and formal rules are given in the course syllabus on OLAT and in this Merkblatt.

You first agree a topic with a supervision person (Bachelor: the supervisor must teach in the Major/Mono programme of the thesis; Master: the supervisor must hold a UZH position in the semester of booking). You must meet all booking prerequisites (check the module description of your study programme) and be validly enrolled with semester fees paid. Book the thesis during the regular online module‑booking/framing deadlines; after the booking deadline you will receive an email to your UZH address to log in and enter the provisional title and supervisor. Submit the final thesis to your supervisor by 1 December (autumn) or 1 June (spring). Late submission = module "not passed" and a failed attempt. After submission you will be asked to enter the definitive title online. In case of impediment before the deadline, request either a short extension or deregister the assessment via the institutes/seminars or the Studienprogrammberatung. Official rules: module descriptions, the UZH module‑booking webpages and institutes/seminars’ web pages.

process.process_description: Enrolled master’s students select a habilitated or equivalently qualified supervisor and agree on a topic. In the semester in which the thesis is submitted the student must book the module “Masterarbeit” via the online module booking system; after the booking deadline an e‑mail requests the provisional title and supervisor and provides the upload link for the final PDF. The thesis is individually written (typically ~50–80 pages, ≈180’000–240’000 characters). It is assessed in two written reports (first reviewer = supervisor; second reviewer appointed by the study commission). Submission: three properly bound copies to Prodekanat Lehre (Büro KIR 106) plus a PDF via the provided upload link. Deadlines: FS 15 May, HS 15 November. Official guidelines and forms (supervision/assessment, declaration of independence, title page, printing specifications) are provided as PDFs on the page.

Bachelorarbeiten werden individuell angefertigt; Umfang ca. 24–30 Seiten (Richtwert 72'000–90'000 Zeichen inkl. Leerzeichen). Studierende wählen eine habilitierte Fachperson des Religionswissenschaftlichen Seminars als Betreuerin/Betreuer. Auf Antrag ist Betreuung, Begutachtung und Benotung auch durch eine habilitierte, am Studiengang beteiligte Fachperson des Theologischen Seminars oder der Philosophischen Fakultät möglich; in diesem Fall erstellt eine habilitierte Fachperson des Religionswissenschaftlichen Seminars das Zweitgutachten. Die Arbeit wird in der Regel in doppelter Ausführung bei der betreuenden Fachperson abgegeben. Als offizielle Hilfsmittel sind ein „Leitfaden zum Verfassen schriftlicher Arbeiten“ (PDF) und die „Selbständigkeitserklärung Bachelorarbeit“ (PDF) verlinkt. Konkrete Angaben zu Anmeldung/Registrierung, Fristen und zum Masterarbeitsverfahren fehlen auf der Seite.

astrophysics.unit: Department of Astrophysics / Institut für Astrophysik

concrete_topics.title: Diversity in the low mass galaxy population
concrete_topics.topic_description: Observations show that low-mass galaxies fall into several broad morphological classes such as ultra-diffuse galaxies, dwarf elliptical galaxies, compact elliptical galaxies, and others. Current numerical models struggle in reproducing this diversity in the low mass galaxy population. The goal of this project is to more robustly quantify this problem and to explore improvements to the modeling to solve this challenge. To this end, we will analyze low-mass galaxies in suites of state-of-the-art cosmological simulations and compare the predicted morphologies, especially their sizes and rotation curves, faithfully with observational data of nearby low-mass galaxies.

concrete_topics.title: Disk galaxy formation
concrete_topics.topic_description: When and how galaxies form stable, thin disks is still not fully understood. A recent model proposes that disk formation is closely linked to the depth of the gravitational potential in the center of galaxies. First, we will test this model prediction and explore its limitations using a large suite of cosmological simulations. Secondly, we will analyze the properties of both the gas and stellar disks in more detail and compare them to available observational data. Finally, we will make predictions for when the first disk galaxies are expected to form in the Universe.

concrete_topics.title: Inferring galaxy properties with Machine Learning
concrete_topics.topic_description: Galaxy properties, such as their masses or star formation rates, are usually observationally inferred from the magnitudes and colors of galaxies. However, interstellar dust can strongly affect these measurements. In many cases, the impact of dust is modeled in a highly simplified and idealized manner which could in principle lead to significant biases in the inferred galaxy properties. In this project, we will use galaxies from a cosmological simulation which have been processed with radiative transfer to quantify these biases and to test how well we can recover intrinsic galaxy properties. As second part, we will train a deep neural network on the simulations to predict intrinsic quantities from mock images and apply it to a real observational data set.

concrete_topics.title: Holes in atomic gas disks
concrete_topics.topic_description: Gas disks of galaxies often show distinct holes which may be created by stellar feedback, turbulence in the interstellar medium, and other processes. The goal of this project is to study holes in the atomic gas disks of simulated galaxies, to quantify their properties, and to determine how they formed. In addition, we will develop a machine learning based classifier to automatically distinguish the different physical origins of holes in atomic gas disks.

concrete_topics.title: Giant planet formation and evolution
concrete_topics.research_area: Planet formation and evolution, planetary interiors, extra-solar planets
concrete_topics.topic_description: Giant planets play a key role in the formation and dynamical evolution of planetary systems. Their origin, however, is still poorly understood. In this project we will use numerical simulations to model the formation and evolution of giant planets with the aim to provide predictions on their compositions and final masses of the planets. We will explore the formation of the outer planets in the solar system as well as of giant exoplanets.

concrete_topics.title: Exoplanet characterization
concrete_topics.research_area: Planet formation and evolution, planetary interiors, extra-solar planets
concrete_topics.topic_description: Planets orbiting other stars are detected at a rapid pace. When both the mass and the radius of a planet are measured, the average density of the planet can be determined. In order to understand what exoplanets are made of, structure models are required. In this project we will characterise exoplanets using interior models, to put limits on their bulk compositions and internal structure, and when possible, link it to their formation and evolution histories.

concrete_topics.title: Giant Impacts of clumps
concrete_topics.research_area: Planet formation and evolution, planetary interiors, extra-solar planets

concrete_topics.title: Constraining Dark Sector with Gravitational Wave from Binary Inspirals
concrete_topics.topic_description: Gravitational waves are detected by merging binary black holes. In the presence of new physics in dark sector beyond the standard model, the gravitational waveform from the inspiral is modified from the standard prediction in general relativity. Here we explore the changes in the gravitational wave signals to the first post-Newtonian order.

concrete_topics.title: Cosmological Observables in the Tetrad Formalism
concrete_topics.topic_description: Cosmological observables such as galaxy clustering, cosmic microwave background anisotropies are measured in the local rest frame of the observers. The tetrad formalism provides a natural way to describe the local observations. The linear order perturbation computations can be performed in the tetrad formalism, connecting the local observables to the cosmological observables in a gauge invariant way.

concrete_topics.title: Pulsar Timing Signatures from Ultra-Light Dark Matter
concrete_topics.topic_description: Recently, international collaborations of pulsar timing array reported evidence for stochastic gravitational wave background. These signals, however, can also come from dark matter in our own Galaxy. The nature of dark matter is poorly understood, and rapidly oscillating light scalar fields as a dark matter candidate can result in rapidly oscillating gravitational potential that can mimic the signals in the pulsar timing array. Here we explore their contributions to PTA signals and ways to distinguish from stochastic gravitational wave background.

concrete_topics.title: Caflisch group
concrete_topics.topic_description: We offer Master thesis projects in computational as well as experimental Biochemistry surrounding the development and validation of small-molecule probes to study proteins involved in epitranscriptomics. In a computational Master Thesis students will carry out a virtual screening campaign for epitranscriptomic targets (docking, MD simulations) and/or develop code (e.g., analysis scripts in Python or R). An experimental Thesis in our group would involve cloning, expression and purification of a protein of interest and binding assays to screen potential ligands (for example by TR-FRET or Fluorescence Anisotropy spectroscopy). Depending on the project and interests of the student, the project could also include testing the activity of small-molecule probes in mammalian cancer cell lines or structure determination of a protein-ligand complex. If you are interested in joining our interdisciplinary group for a Master Thesis, please contact Prof. A. Caflisch ( caflisch@bioc.uzh.ch ).

concrete_topics.title: Dutzler group
concrete_topics.topic_description: Structural biology of regulatory domains in ion transport proteins Ion transport proteins are frequently regulated by extramembraneous ligand binding domains. The project includes the cloning expression crystallization and structure determination of the isolated domain of an ion transport protein.

concrete_topics.topic_description: Master thesis projects are available in the entire range of topics investigated in the group. Please see the website for general information on our research and recent publications, and contact schuler@bioc.uzh.ch concerning details and availability.

concrete_topics.title: Interdisciplinary MSc Thesis on chemical innovation
concrete_topics.topic_description: This MSc thesis evaluates the role of chemical persistence testing in pharmaceutical drug development, aiming to identify current practices, drivers and barriers to implementation and to assess how novel high-throughput methods can enable earlier, more sustainable chemical design. The student will conduct a literature review and market analysis, do a hands-on placement at Eawag to learn a newly developed rapid persistence testing method, and carry out industry interviews to assess firm-level drivers and barriers. The project will synthesize technical, socio-economic and political factors to describe opportunities and limitations for advancing persistence testing standards in the pharmaceutical industry.

concrete_topics.title: Master Thesis in Environmental Chemistry: Environmental Risk Assessment of 6PPD and its Alternatives
concrete_topics.topic_description: The project aims to elucidate potential environmental hazards of 6PPD alternatives used in tires by identifying their transformation pathways and any toxic transformation products. The student will carry out medium-scale abiotic and biotic transformation and sorption experiments, measure and model transformation kinetics, predict transformation products, and perform targeted and non-targeted HR-MS/MS searches using Skyline/Tracefinder. Measured HR‑MS data will be analyzed with R/Python and the MLinvitroTox tool to explore toxicity pathways and generate a first environmental risk assessment of the alternatives; experimental work will be conducted at Eawag (Dübendorf).

concrete_topics.title: MSc Thesis in Biochemistry
concrete_topics.topic_description: This project investigates novel Group II intron candidates that may self-splice and insert into genomes using an encoded reverse transcriptase (RVT). You will confirm self-splicing with ribozyme activity assays, identify intron structural elements by footprinting assays, and test for potential retro homing in the presence of the RVT. Work involves in vitro transcription, protein purification and RNA biochemistry; training and integration into an interdisciplinary team will be provided.

concrete_topics.title: MSc about Artificial Enzymes
concrete_topics.topic_description: Develop novel, sustainable catalysts by integrating metal complexes into protein scaffolds to create artificial enzymes. The student will synthesize metal‑catalyst@protein complexes, perform protein engineering to incorporate and optimize the metal centres, and characterize their catalytic behaviour using electrochemistry and catalytic assays. The project is hands‑on and interdisciplinary, involving close collaboration across two research groups.

concrete_topics.title: MSc in Biomolecular NMR
concrete_topics.topic_description: This MSc thesis aims to uncover the structural and dynamic basis for the large differences in self‑cleavage activity caused by single‑point mutations in theta ribozymes by comparing variants to the original sequence using NMR spectroscopy. The student will prepare RNA by in vitro transcription and use NMR to assess structural homogeneity and conformational dynamics of mutants versus wild type, correlating subtle changes in helices and base pairs with catalytic performance. The project involves learning NMR techniques and NMR data analysis applied to RNA biochemistry.

concrete_topics.title: MSc Thesis in Biochemistry/Bioinorganic Chemistry
concrete_topics.topic_description: The project aims to characterize Zn2+-induced liquid–liquid phase separation of an intrinsically disordered zinc-sensor protein from Arabidopsis thaliana (including a series of mutants) to build a mechanistic model of metal-induced phase separation, and to investigate the mechanism of metal transfer between this sensor and metallothioneins. The student will express, isotopically label and purify proteins and use UV–Vis, MALDI‑MS, NMR, ITC and biochemical assays to map metal binding and transfer, performing daily experimental work, precise lab techniques and presenting results in group meetings.

concrete_topics.title: MSc Thesis in Biochemistry/Bioinorganic Chemistry
concrete_topics.topic_description: This MSc project will determine how hyperphosphorylation modulates metal binding and reversible Zn2+-induced liquid–liquid phase separation of an intrinsically disordered Arabidopsis thaliana protein. You will optimize protein expression and purification to produce sufficient phosphorylated protein, then characterize how phosphorylation alters metal binding and phase behavior using UV-Vis, MALDI‑MS, NMR, ITC, DLS, fluorescence microscopy and biochemical assays. The work involves daily hands-on protein biochemistry/biophysics, precise experimental work, and presenting results in group meetings.

concrete_topics.title: Master Thesis in Physical Chemistry / Biochemistry
concrete_topics.topic_description: This project aims to characterize intrinsically disordered proteins and regions that regulate the two major cell‑cycle checkpoints using NMR spectroscopy to illuminate their structure–function relationships. The student will optimize recombinant expression of IDRs/IDPs with advanced isotopic labeling, perform protein expression and purification, collect and analyze NMR data, and apply complementary biophysical techniques (BLI, CD).

concrete_topics.title: MSc Thesis in Medicinal Inorganic Chemistry (2)
concrete_topics.topic_description: This MSc project aims to develop novel Fe(III) complexes as anticancer agents that selectively release inside cancer cells and are reduced to Fe(II), triggering Fenton-type reactions to generate reactive oxygen species and induce cell death. The student will design and synthesize these complexes, develop analytical assays, and perform biological evaluation with cell studies carried out in collaboration.

concrete_topics.title: MSc Thesis in Medicinal Inorganic Chemistry (1)
concrete_topics.topic_description: This MSc project aims to design, synthesize and evaluate novel metal–corrin complexes as potential anticancer agents with high efficacy and minimal side effects. The student will synthesize metal–corrin complexes, characterize their fundamental properties (including electrochemistry), and perform biological evaluation with cell studies carried out in collaboration.
